sentences.en: And maybe it takes them a few decades to forge this new kind of society, one in which the drive for honour is something that can be turned against Rome's neighbours.
sentences.zh: 也许他们花了几十年时间来打造这种新型社会，在这个社会中，对荣誉的追求可以转变成对抗罗马邻国的力量。

sentences.en: Well, by the 340s, all the Latin cities around Rome have been utterly subordinated to Roman authority.
sentences.zh: 好吧，到了公元前340年代，罗马周边的所有拉丁城市都完全臣服于罗马的权威。

sentences.en: Lots of them have been enrolled within the citizen body of Rome itself.
sentences.zh: 其中许多城市已被纳入罗马本身的公民群体中。

sentences.en: What happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: How does this reliance upon force that Polybius identifies, how does it manifest itself in the context of Italian politics?
sentences.zh: 波利比乌斯所指出的这种对武力的依赖，在意大利政治的背景下是如何体现的？

sentences.en: So, south of Latium, of the land of the Latins, there is Campania, which is Naples, Capua, both of them Greek cities, Pompeii, sheltering under Mount Vesuvius, rich, prosperous,
sentences.zh: 因此，在拉丁姆（即拉丁人土地）以南，是坎帕尼亚，那里有那不勒斯、卡普亚（两者都是希腊城市），还有在维苏威火山庇护下的庞贝，富饶、繁荣，

sentences.en: civilised.
sentences.zh: 文明。

sentences.en: But up in the mountains, you have a people called the Samnites, very hardy warriors, whose ancestors supposedly were led there from not far from Rome by,
sentences.zh: 但是在山里，有一个叫做萨姆尼特人的民族，他们是非常强悍的战士，据传说，他们的祖先是由离罗马不远的地方被，

sentences.en: depending on who told the story, a bull or a wolf or a woodpecker.
sentences.zh: 根据讲故事的人不同，由一头公牛、一匹狼或一只啄木鸟引领到那里的。

sentences.en: God, you wouldn't want to be led by a woodpecker, would you?
sentences.zh: 天哪，你可不想被一只啄木鸟引领，对吧？

sentences.en: I'd choose the wolf.
sentences.zh: 我会选择狼。

sentences.en: I think I would.
sentences.zh: 我想我会的。

sentences.en: I was thinking about this.
sentences.zh: 我一直在想这个。

sentences.en: I think I would choose, because at least you wouldn't lose him, would you?
sentences.zh: 我想我会选择，因为至少你不会弄丢它，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you'd always be able to hear him knocking on a tree.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你总是能听到它在敲树。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's so demeaning, you know, I think a bull, fine, but a wolf is better, and a woodpecker is definitely a third.
sentences.zh: 对，但这太有失身份了，你知道的，我觉得公牛挺好，但狼更好，而啄木鸟绝对排在第三位。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样。

sentences.en: Okay, so you're not team woodpecker.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以你不是啄木鸟战队的。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Anyway, so these are people who are viewed, even by the Romans, as being very, very savage.
sentences.zh: 总之，这些人甚至被罗马人视为非常非常野蛮。

sentences.en: They're notorious for practising witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 他们以行巫术而闻名。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: They wear great heavy rings of iron around their neck, and they're supposedly given to shaving their private parts in public.
sentences.zh: 他们脖子上戴着沉重的铁环，据说还有在公共场合剃掉自己私处毛发的习惯。

sentences.en: Again, this is the woodpecker issue, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 说到底，这又是啄木鸟的问题了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, this is what happens when you go down that road.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，这就是你走那条路的结果。

sentences.en: And they will live long in the Roman imagination, you know, for centuries afterwards, because they are given to wearing very thick belts and helmets with great bobbing crests.
sentences.zh: 他们在罗马人的想象中留下了长久的印象，你知道的，持续了几个世纪，因为他们习惯佩戴非常厚重的腰带和带有高高晃动羽饰的头盔。

sentences.en: And this is a style that will become very popular with gladiators.
sentences.zh: 这种风格后来在角斗士中非常流行。

sentences.en: So you think the classic image of the gladiator with its bobbing crest and its great big belt.
sentences.zh: 所以你认为角斗士的经典形象，带着晃动的羽饰和硕大的腰带。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is Samnite armour.
sentences.zh: 这就是萨姆尼特人的盔甲。

sentences.en: And so they are viewed by, certainly, the people down in the plains of Campania with contempt.
sentences.zh: 所以，坎帕尼亚平原上的人们当然对他们充满了蔑视。

sentences.en: Not unreasonably, I would say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得这并不不合理。

sentences.en: So the Greeks particularly.
sentences.zh: 因此尤其是希腊人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so the very hostile relations between Samnites and the Campanians.
sentences.zh: 所以萨姆尼特人和坎帕尼亚人之间的敌对关系非常严重。

sentences.en: The Samnites are always coming down, trying to kind of bully and intimidate the Capuans or the Neapolitans, kind of go off with their cattle, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 萨姆尼特人总是来这里，试图霸凌和恐吓卡普阿人或那不勒斯人，顺便抢走他们的牛之类的东西。

sentences.en: And so in the second half of the fourth century, the Romans, who are now the great power in central Italy, get sucked into this.
sentences.zh: 因此，在公元前四世纪下半叶，如今已成为意大利中部超级大国的罗马人也被卷入了这场冲突。

sentences.en: And they kind of come in on the side of Capua.
sentences.zh: 他们算是站在了卡普阿一边。

sentences.en: They start fighting against the Samnites.
sentences.zh: 他们开始与萨姆尼特人作战。

sentences.en: They then get distracted by the Latin uprising.
sentences.zh: 随后他们又被拉丁起义分散了注意力。

sentences.en: And when they resume hostilities in 341, the Samnites immediately come to terMs.
sentences.zh: 当他们在公元前341年恢复敌对状态时，萨姆尼特人立即言和。

sentences.en: The Romans patch up an alliance with the Samnites.
sentences.zh: 罗马人与萨姆尼特人修好了同盟关系。

sentences.en: The Campanians are now siding with the Latins.
sentences.zh: 坎帕尼亚人现在则站在了拉丁人一边。

sentences.en: It's all very confusing.
sentences.zh: 这一切非常混乱。

sentences.en: But I think what is obvious from this kind of whole confusing melange of Romans fighting Samnites on behalf of the Campanians and the Campanians are then fighting with the Latins against them.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，从这整个令人眼花缭乱的大杂烩中可以明显看出：罗马人代表坎帕尼亚人与萨姆尼特人作战，而坎帕尼亚人随后又与拉丁人一起对抗罗马人。

sentences.en: I mean, it's all incredibly Balkan.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直太巴尔干化了。

sentences.en: What's clear is that the Romans are basically going to be going to war with the Samnites.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的是，罗马人基本上将与萨姆尼特人开战。

sentences.en: And so it turns out, because in 326, war blazes out again.
sentences.zh: 事实确实如此，因为在公元前326年，战争再次爆发了。

sentences.en: And this will last for 22 years.
sentences.zh: 这场战争将持续22年。

sentences.en: And the Romans carry it on, despite the fact that they suffer one of their most humiliating defeats, when they get trapped in a narrow valley called the Cordine Forks.
sentences.zh: 尽管罗马人遭遇了他们最耻辱的失败之一——他们被困在了一个叫考丁峡谷的狭窄山谷里，但他们依然将战争进行到底。

sentences.en: And the Sabines, rather than massacring them, they play by the rules, because there are accepted rules in Italian warfare.
sentences.zh: 萨姆尼特人并没有屠杀他们，而是按规矩办事，因为当时意大利战争中有公认的规则。

sentences.en: If you capture your enemy, you know, you force them to submit.
sentences.zh: 如果你俘虏了敌人，你知道的，你会迫使他们屈服。

sentences.en: So you make a yoke, you have two spears stuck in the ground, and then you put another spear across it.
sentences.zh: 所以你要做一个轭，把两根长矛插在地上，然后在上面横放另一根长矛。

sentences.en: And the defeated army has to thread beneath this yoke.
sentences.zh: 战败的军队必须从这个轭下钻过去。

sentences.en: They have to agree to end the war, and they have to accept the terms of the conqueror.
sentences.zh: 他们必须同意结束战争，并且必须接受征服者的条件。

sentences.en: So in this context, after the defeat of the Cordine Forks, two Roman consuls who had been in charge of the army agree that they will withdraw what the Romans called coloniae,
sentences.zh: 因此在这种背景下，在考丁峡谷战败后，曾统帅军队的两名罗马执政官同意撤回罗马人所谓的“殖民地”（coloniae），

sentences.en: which are colonies, the English word comes from, which are kind of plantations of Romans in enemy territory.
sentences.zh: 也就是殖民地，英文单词就是这么来的，这基本上是在敌方领土上建立的罗马人据点。

sentences.en: So the Romans have planted coloniae in Samnium, and the condition of their army being allowed to go is that they will withdraw this,
sentences.zh: 所以罗马人在萨姆尼姆建立了殖民地，而放他们军队离开的条件就是撤回这些殖民地，

sentences.en: and they swear this to the gods and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们向神明发誓并进行了诸如此类的种种仪式。

sentences.en: But what about this thing about the Romans would endure any suffering rather than be humiliated?
sentences.zh: 但是关于“罗马人宁可忍受任何苦难也绝不接受羞辱”这种说法呢？

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: So when the defeated legions come down from Samnium into Campania, they're too humiliated even to show their faces in Capua.
sentences.zh: 因此，当战败的军团从萨姆尼姆撤回坎帕尼亚时，他们感到羞耻得甚至不敢在卡普阿露面。

sentences.en: They're so embarrassed, they feel they've let the Capuans down, they've let the Romans down, but worst of all, they've let themselves down.
sentences.zh: 他们感到如此尴尬，觉得辜负了卡普阿人，辜负了罗马人，但最糟糕的是，他们辜负了自己。

sentences.en: And when they get back home to Rome, they just go and lock themselves up in their homes and won't come out.
sentences.zh: 当他们回到罗马的家中时，他们只是把自己锁在屋里，怎么也不肯出来。

sentences.en: And so the shame of this is something that is clearly insufferable.
sentences.zh: 这种耻辱显然是难以忍受的。

sentences.en: And so one of the consuls who has agreed to the terms stands up in the Senate and says, look, guys, it was me and my consular colleague who agreed this.
sentences.zh: 于是，一位同意了这些条件的执政官在元老院站出来说：听着，各位，是我和我的执政官同僚同意了这些。

sentences.en: You, the Roman people, did not agree this.
sentences.zh: 你们，罗马人民，并没有同意这一点。

sentences.en: So you can carry on the war.
sentences.zh: 所以你们可以继续战争。

sentences.en: Of course, this will require me and my colleague to be handed over naked and shackled to the Samnites.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就需要我和我的同僚赤身裸体、戴着镣铐被交还给萨姆尼特人。

sentences.en: But because we are patriotic Romans, we are willing to accept that.
sentences.zh: 但因为我们是热爱祖国的罗马人，我们愿意接受这一点。

sentences.en: And so this is what happens.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样发生了。

sentences.en: The Romans return to war.
sentences.zh: 罗马人重返战场。

sentences.en: The consuls are given to the Samnites.
sentences.zh: 执政官被交给了萨姆尼特人。

sentences.en: The Samnites don't know what to do with them, so send them back because they're still playing by the traditional rules.
sentences.zh: 萨姆尼特人不知道该拿他们怎么办，于是把他们送了回去，因为他们仍然在遵守传统的规则。

sentences.en: And the Romans embark on a kind of total war, endless grueling sequence of campaigns.
sentences.zh: 罗马人随后展开了一场全面战争，开启了无休止、折磨人的漫长战役。

sentences.en: But by 304, the Samnites, you know, they have no choice but to sue for terMs.
sentences.zh: 但到了公元前304年，萨姆尼特人别无选择，只能求和。

sentences.en: There's another cycle of war that breaks out in 298.
sentences.zh: 公元前298年爆发了新一轮的战争周期。

sentences.en: But by 290, the Samnites have been decisively defeated.
sentences.zh: 但到公元前290年，萨姆尼特人已经被决定性地击败。

sentences.en: Roman colonies are planted across their land.
sentences.zh: 罗马殖民地遍布他们的土地。

sentences.en: The Samnites themselves are forced to become allies of Rome.
sentences.zh: 萨姆尼特人自己也被迫成为罗马的盟友。

sentences.en: Much of their land is annexed.
sentences.zh: 他们的大片土地被吞并。

sentences.en: And essentially, the Samnites are now being absorbed into the apparatus of the Roman war machine.
sentences.zh: 本质上，萨姆尼特人现在被并入了罗马战争机器的体制中。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, even as the Romans have been fighting the Samnites, they've also been going northwards, attacking the Etruscan cities, conquering them,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，甚至在与萨姆尼特人作战的同时，罗马人也在向北推进，攻击伊特鲁里亚人的城市，征服他们，

sentences.en: absorbing them into their framework of alliances.
sentences.zh: 并将他们纳入罗马的同盟体系中。

sentences.en: Even the Gauls in the north of Italy are being forced to submit.
sentences.zh: 甚至意大利北部的凯尔特人（高卢人）也被迫屈服。

sentences.en: And by 285, so this is, you know, within the lifetime since that treaty with Carthage was signed, the Romans have conquered pretty much the whole of Italy.
sentences.zh: 到了公元前285年，也就是自从与迦太基签署那份条约以来的有生之年里，罗马人几乎征服了整个意大利。

sentences.en: And all that remains really independent is the Greek cities in the south.
sentences.zh: 真正保持独立的只有南部的希腊城市。

sentences.en: So Magna Graeca, as the Romans called it.
sentences.zh: 也就是罗马人所说的“大希腊”。

sentences.en: So to just pause a second and look to Carthage.
sentences.zh: 让我们暂停一下，把目光转向迦太基。

sentences.en: The Carthaginians at that point do not have colonies and territories on the mainland of Italy and never have?
sentences.zh: 当时的迦太基人在意大利本土没有殖民地和领土，而且从来都没有吗？

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: They have trading colonies.
sentences.zh: 他们有贸易殖民地。

sentences.en: So they're kind of like...
sentences.zh: 所以它们有点像……

sentences.en: Sort of Hong Kong and Singapore type places.
sentences.zh: 类似于香港和新加坡那样的地方。

sentences.en: Not exactly, because they're not administered by the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 不完全是，因为它们不受迦太基人管理。

sentences.en: But there are kind of colonies of Carthaginian merchants within all these various cities.
sentences.zh: 但在所有这些不同的城市里，都有某种迦太基商人的聚居地。

sentences.en: And that is what the treaties have agreed to.
sentences.zh: 这就是条约所约定的内容。

sentences.en: But they haven't been conquered by the Romans?
sentences.zh: 但它们没有被罗马人征服吗？

sentences.en: Or they have?
sentences.zh: 还是说已经被征服了？

sentences.en: They have been conquered by the Romans, yeah.
sentences.zh: 它们已经被罗马人征服了，是的。

sentences.en: But the Romans are just letting the Carthaginian merchants in those places crack on with it.
sentences.zh: 但罗马人只是让那些地方的迦太基商人继续做他们自己的事。

sentences.en: Yes, because the Romans' treaty with Carthage provides for cities that are dominated by Rome.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为罗马与迦太基的条约顾及了那些受罗马支配的城市。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So the provisions of the treaty with Rome now governs the whole of Italy.
sentences.zh: 所以与罗马条约的条款现在管辖着整个意大利。

sentences.en: Understood.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So Rome and Carthage are still allies at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以此时罗马和迦太基仍然是盟友。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And actually, the fact that Rome is now gearing up to attack the Greek colonies in the south of Italy, the area that had been settled, much as Sicily had been,
sentences.zh: 事实上，罗马现在正准备攻击意大利南部的希腊殖民地——这一地区和西西里岛一样，曾被殖民，

sentences.en: southern Italy also had been settled by Greek colonists.
sentences.zh: 意大利南部也曾有希腊殖民者定居。

sentences.en: The Greeks are the enemies of the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 希腊人是迦太基人的敌人。

sentences.en: The Romans are now having a crack at the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 而罗马人现在正在向希腊人发起进攻。

sentences.en: So there's every reason for the Carthaginians and the Romans still to be allies.
sentences.zh: 因此，迦太基人和罗马人完全有理由继续保持同盟关系。

sentences.en: And the most powerful Greek city in the south is Tarentum, founded by the Spartans many, many centuries before and preserving that kind of military tradition.
sentences.zh: 南部最强大的希腊城市是塔兰托，它在几个世纪前由斯巴达人建立，并一直保留着这种军事传统。

sentences.en: But the Romans are clearly too powerful for the Tarentines on their own to resiSt.
sentences.zh: 但罗马人显然太强大了，塔兰托人单凭自己根本无法抵抗。

sentences.en: And so they look around for an ally.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始寻找盟友。

sentences.en: And fortunately for the Tarentines, such an ally is there just on the other side of the Adriatic in the mountainous kingdom of Epirus, kind of around Albania, that kind of area.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是对于塔兰托人来说，这样一个盟友就在亚得里亚海的另一边，位于伊庇鲁斯的多山王国，大约在阿尔巴尼亚那种地方。

sentences.en: And its king is a guy called Pyrrhus.
sentences.zh: 它的国王是一个叫皮洛士的人。

sentences.en: Okay, I hope he doesn't win a Pyrrhic victory, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好吧，希望他不要赢得“皮洛士式的胜利”，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, so Pyrrhus is, he's very much an Alexander the Great wannabe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以皮洛士这个人，他非常渴望成为亚历山大大帝第二。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's stuck in this kind of mountainous sub-Macedonian kingdom.
sentences.zh: 他被困在这个类似马其顿下属的多山王国里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he wants scope for glory.
sentences.zh: 他渴望获得展现荣耀的机会。

sentences.en: And he's a very, very proficient general.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常非常出色的将军。

sentences.en: He's been kind of swaggering around the eastern Mediterranean, scoring all kinds of victories.
sentences.zh: 他曾在东地中海一带耀武扬威，赢得了各种胜利。

sentences.en: But he does have links to the west because he's married to the daughter of Agathocles, who's a tyrant of Syracuse.
sentences.zh: 但他确实与西方有联系，因为他娶了叙古萨（锡拉库萨）暴君阿加托克利斯的女儿。

sentences.en: Who we talked about in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集里聊过的那个人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So when the invitation from the Tarentines come, Pyrrhus looks over, he thinks, yeah, southern Italy, Sicily, scope here for glory.
sentences.zh: 所以当塔兰托人的邀请到来时，皮洛士放眼望去，心想：没错，意大利南部，西西里岛，这里有获取荣耀的空间。

sentences.en: And so he crosses the Adriatic with an enormous army that features, for the first time in Italian combat, war elephants.
sentences.zh: 于是他率领着一支庞大的军队横渡亚得里亚海，这支军队中首次在意大利战场上出现了战象。

sentences.en: Okay, can we stop, talk about the elephants for a second?
sentences.zh: 好的，我们能停一下，聊聊大象的事吗？

sentences.en: Because I love an elephant on the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 因为我在《历史余音》（The Rest is History）里太喜欢大象了。

sentences.en: The elephants he has presumably got, because as king of Epirus, he, and part of the kind of Macedonian Hellenistic world.
sentences.zh: 他拥有的大象据推测是因为，作为伊庇鲁斯国王，他属于马其顿希腊化世界的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He presumably has got those from the Seleucids, from the Greek Empire in Asia.
sentences.zh: 他大概是从塞琉古王朝、从亚洲的希腊帝国那里弄来的那些大象。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm guessing.
sentences.zh: 我猜的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They've come from India.
sentences.zh: 它们来自印度。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's a great deep water port on the Red Sea where vast ships come with elephants.
sentences.zh: 红海边有一个很棒的深水港，那里有巨型船只运送大象。

sentences.en: And basically you can source elephants from there, or you can source elephants from the kings in Syria who have access kind of across the land channels.
sentences.zh: 基本上你可以从那里获取大象，或者你可以从叙利亚那些通过陆路通道获得大象的国王那里获取。

sentences.en: So yeah, this is how you get elephants.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这就是你获得大象的方式。

sentences.en: Or there's a particular kind of elephant that is now extinct that is in North Africa.
sentences.zh: 或者还有一种现在已经灭绝的特殊大象，生活在北非。

sentences.en: So this is where the Carthaginians get their elephants.
sentences.zh: 这就是迦太基人获得大象的地方。

sentences.en: Is that so?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So elephants are available if you want them.
sentences.zh: 所以只要你想要，大象是能弄到的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And why wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 而且你为什么不想要呢？

sentences.en: And Pyrrhus does want them.
sentences.zh: 皮洛士确实想要。

sentences.en: Right, right too.
sentences.zh: 对，太对了。

sentences.en: Because, of course, horses are terrified of elephants.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，马非常害怕大象。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, cavalry charging along and you see an elephant and they all go screaming off in reverse.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，骑兵正在冲锋，突然看到一头大象，它们就会尖叫着掉头逃跑。

sentences.en: And, of course, they can go crashing into a line of infantry, stampede them.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，大象可以冲进步兵方阵，把他们踩踏得溃不成军。

sentences.en: Terrifying.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: The issue with elephants, Tom, I know we're not the rest is military history,
sentences.zh: 关于大象的问题，汤姆，我知道我们不是在讲军事历史，

sentences.en: but I believe the issue with elephants is that elephants can easily be frightened and will stampede their own side.
sentences.zh: 但据我所知，大象的问题在于它们很容易受到惊吓，并且会践踏自己一方的军队。

sentences.en: That is constantly a risk.
sentences.zh: 这始终是一个风险。

sentences.en: So they can be a tremendous liability.
sentences.zh: 所以它们可能是一个巨大的累赘。

sentences.en: They can be.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But if you're a top general like Pyrrhus, you know how to control them.
sentences.zh: 但如果你像皮洛士一样是一位顶级将军，你就知道如何控制它们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so Pyrrhus in 280, he lands in Italy and he brings a whole load of war elephants.
sentences.zh: 因此皮洛士在公元前280年登陆意大利，他带来了大量战象。

sentences.en: He brings his cavalry.
sentences.zh: 他带来了他的骑兵。

sentences.en: Macedonian cavalry is famous.
sentences.zh: 马其顿骑兵闻名遐迩。

sentences.en: And, of course, he brings his phalanx, you know, enormously long spears, the instrument of war that had enabled Alexander to conquer the Persian Empire.
sentences.zh: 当然，他还带来了他的方阵，你知道的，拥有极长的长矛，正是这种战争工具让亚历山大征服了波斯帝国。

sentences.en: Tremendous innovation.
sentences.zh: 巨大的创新。

sentences.en: So the Romans are now in the big league.
sentences.zh: 所以罗马人现在进入了顶级联赛。

sentences.en: I mean, again, to pursue the football analogy, this is the Champions League.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，继续用足球来打比方，这就是欧冠联赛。

sentences.en: They are now facing the most terrifying way of making war that exists in the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 他们现在面对的是地中海地区存在的最可怕的作战方式。

sentences.en: How are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 他们将如何应对？

sentences.en: Well, they meet at a place called Heraclia, the Romans and Pyrrhus's army, which is in southern Italy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，罗马人和皮洛士的军队在一个叫赫拉克利亚的地方相遇了，这个地方在意大利南部。

sentences.en: And the elephants are brought out.
sentences.zh: 大象被派上场了。

sentences.en: The Roman horses are terrified.
sentences.zh: 罗马人的战马吓坏了。

sentences.en: They scarper.
sentences.zh: 它们逃跑了。

sentences.en: The Romans lose.
sentences.zh: 罗马人输了。

sentences.en: But it's a very bloody victory.
sentences.zh: 但这是一场代价惨重的胜利。

sentences.en: The Romans inflict a lot of casualties on Pyrrhus.
sentences.zh: 罗马人为皮洛士造成了大量伤亡。

sentences.en: And so Pyrrhus is also playing by the rules.
sentences.zh: 因此，皮洛士也是按规矩行事的。

sentences.en: You know, he doesn't want to conquer Rome and destroy it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他并不想征服罗马并摧毁它。

sentences.en: He assumes that having won his victory, the Romans will now negotiate.
sentences.zh: 他认为既然赢得了胜利，罗马人现在就会进行谈判。

sentences.en: And so he sends an embassy to Rome and he offers, yeah, very reasonable terMs.
sentences.zh: 于是他派了一个使团去罗马，并且提出了非常合理的条件。

sentences.en: So he says, you know, I'll free the prisoners that I've taken.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，我会释放我俘虏的战俘。

sentences.en: I'll help you with the subjugation of the rest of Italy.
sentences.zh: 我会帮你们征服意大利的其他地区。

sentences.en: All you've got to do is give immunity to Tarentum.
sentences.zh: 你们只需要给予塔兰托免责权就行了。

sentences.en: And the Senate is tempted to accept these terMs.
sentences.zh: 而元老院很想接受这些条件。

sentences.en: I mean, they seem very good.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们看起来非常好。

sentences.en: But then you have, you know, this terrifyingly craggy old senator who is a Claudian, Appius Claudius.
sentences.zh: 但接着你有了这样一个可怕而顽固的老参议员，他是一个克劳迪亚斯家族的人，阿皮乌斯·克劳迪乌斯。

sentences.en: And he is the guy who builds the Appian Way, the great road that runs from Rome down to the heel of Italy.
sentences.zh: 他是建造阿庇亚大道的人，那是从罗马一直延伸到意大利鞋跟部的大道。

sentences.en: And which is like a kind of a chain that has been cast over the mountains of Samnium, enabling the Romans to strike where they want.
sentences.zh: 它就像一条被投放在萨姆尼姆群山之上的铁链，使罗马人能够随心所欲地发起攻击。

sentences.en: And he is blind.
sentences.zh: 而且他是盲人。

sentences.en: So he's called Caicus, the blind.
sentences.zh: 所以他被称为卡伊库斯，即盲人。

sentences.en: And he stands up and he basically says, never surrender.
sentences.zh: 他站起来，基本上说，绝不投降。

sentences.en: We are never going to negotiate with an invader of Italy.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会与一个入侵意大利的敌人谈判。

sentences.en: And he has this famous line, every man is the architect of his own destiny, with the implication that every citizen has it within him to be the architect of Rome's destiny.
sentences.zh: 他有这句名言：每个人都是自己命运的建筑师，其含义是每个公民内心都有能力成为罗马命运的建筑师。

sentences.en: And so the Romans carry on the fight.
sentences.zh: 于是罗马人继续战斗。

sentences.en: The following year, 279, there's another battle, another victory for Pyrrhus.
sentences.zh: 次年，即公元前279年，又发生了一场战役，皮洛士再次获胜。

sentences.en: But again, his phalanx, his cavalry, his elephants are very, very badly maimed.
sentences.zh: 但他的方阵、骑兵和战象再次受到了非常惨重的创伤。

sentences.en: And it's at this point that he makes the famous comment, another victory like this, and it will be the ruin of me.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，他留下了那句名言：再有一次这样的胜利，我可就彻底完蛋了。

sentences.en: So this is exactly where the phrase Pyrrhic victory comes from.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是“皮洛士式的胜利”这个短语的由来。

sentences.en: And he decides he's had enough.
sentences.zh: 他决定他受够了。

sentences.en: He thinks, you know, I don't want to keep fighting the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他想，你知道的，我不想再和罗马人打下去了。

sentences.en: I won't have anybody left.
sentences.zh: 我身边一个人都不会剩下了。

sentences.en: And so he goes off to Sicily to fight the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 于是他前往西西里去对抗迦太基人。

sentences.en: He's invited there by the Sicilian Greeks.
sentences.zh: 他是应西西里希腊人的邀请而去的。

sentences.en: They want another Greek to help them have a crack at the Carthaginians, which they're always doing.
sentences.zh: 他们想要另一个希腊人来帮他们教训一下迦太基人，他们总是这么做。

sentences.en: And Pyrrhus is keen to install his grandson, who is Agathocles' grandson as well, because Pyrrhus has married Agathocles' daughter, to become king of Syracuse.
sentences.zh: 而皮洛士热衷于让他的孙子——同时也是阿加托克利斯的孙子，因为皮洛士娶了阿加托克利斯的女儿——成为叙拉古的国王。

sentences.en: So basically, he's trying to establish, you know, his dynasty in Syracuse.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他是在试图在叙拉古建立他的王朝。

sentences.en: So he goes off and does that.
sentences.zh: 于是他去了并做了那件事。

sentences.en: But Pyrrhus, unfortunately, behaves in such a kind of arrogant manner that all the Greeks get pissed off with him.
sentences.zh: 但遗憾的是，皮洛士的行为如此傲慢，以至于所有的希腊人都对他感到恼火。

sentences.en: And they switch sides and team up with the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 他们临阵倒戈，与迦太基人结盟。

sentences.en: So Pyrrhus and the Greeks have split up.
sentences.zh: 因此，皮洛士和希腊人分道扬镳了。

sentences.en: So Pyrrhus now finds himself fighting both the Carthaginians and the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 所以皮洛士现在发现自己同时在与迦太基人和希腊人作战。

sentences.en: And he thinks, you know, had enough of this.
sentences.zh: 他想，你知道的，受够了这一切。

sentences.en: So he heads back to Italy.
sentences.zh: 于是他动身返回意大利。

sentences.en: But there he finds that the Romans have built up their forces, inevitably.
sentences.zh: 但他在那里发现，罗马人不可避免地已经增兵了。

sentences.en: There's another battle.
sentences.zh: 又发生了一场战役。

sentences.en: Again, it's indecisive.
sentences.zh: 结果依然是不分胜负。

sentences.en: Again, the Romans inflict devastating casualties on Pyrrhus.
sentences.zh: 罗马人再次给皮洛士造成了毁灭性的伤亡。

sentences.en: And he decides that he's had enough.
sentences.zh: 他决定他受够了。

sentences.en: And so he packs up and goes home.
sentences.zh: 于是他收拾行装回国了。

sentences.en: And that basically is the last that Pyrrhus is engaged in Italy.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是皮洛士在意大利的最后干预了。

sentences.en: And in 272, he goes off into southern Greece, into the Peloponnese.
sentences.zh: 在公元前272年，他前往希腊南部，进入伯罗奔尼撒半岛。

sentences.en: He gets involved in a street battle in Argos.
sentences.zh: 他卷入了阿尔戈斯的一场街头巷战。

sentences.en: And he's fighting with this guy.
sentences.zh: 他正在和一个家伙搏斗。

sentences.en: And the guy's mother is up on the roof, you know, sees her beloved boy fighting Pyrrhus.
sentences.zh: 那个家伙的母亲在屋顶上，你知道的，看到她心爱的儿子在跟皮洛士拼杀。

sentences.en: Reaches for a roof tile, hurls it at Pyrrhus, brains him, and it kills him.
sentences.zh: 她顺手抓起一块屋顶瓦片，朝皮洛士砸过去，正中他的脑门，把他当场砸死了。

sentences.en: And so that's the end of Pyrrhus.
sentences.zh: 这就是皮洛士的结局。

sentences.en: What a depressing end for Pyrrhus.
sentences.zh: 皮洛士的结局真是令人沮丧。

sentences.en: Yeah, very sad.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常悲惨。

sentences.en: Very rich to the Lionheart.
sentences.zh: 对狮心王来说非常丰富。

sentences.en: But meanwhile, back in Italy, the moment he goes, the Romans move into Tarentum, take it.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，在意大利，他一走，罗马人就开进塔兰托并占领了它。

sentences.en: And basically, the conquest of Italy is complete.
sentences.zh: 基本上，对意大利的征服完成了。

sentences.en: Just one thing on Pyrrhus.
sentences.zh: 关于皮洛士，还有最后一件事。

sentences.en: All that stuff about the Romans being invincible and brilliant and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所有关于罗马人战无不胜、极其聪明之类的话。

sentences.en: I mean, they didn't be Pyrrhus.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们没有击败皮洛士。

sentences.en: Pyrrhus won.
sentences.zh: 皮洛士赢了。

sentences.en: No, they didn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他们没有。

sentences.en: But Pyrrhus, yes, he does effectively win three battles, but he doesn't win the war because the Romans keep coming back.
sentences.zh: 但是皮洛士，是的，他确实实际上赢了三场战役，但他并没有赢得战争，因为罗马人不断卷土重来。

sentences.en: And it's not that the Romans expect to win every battle, but they expect to win every war.
sentences.zh: 并不是说罗马人指望赢得每一场战役，而是他们指望赢得每一场战争。

sentences.en: Right, because of their manpower, Tom.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为他们的人力资源，汤姆。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter how many battles they lose, they will always come back.
sentences.zh: 不管他们输掉多少场战役，他们总是会卷土重来。

sentences.en: And this, of course, will be a key theme in the wars that Rome goes on to fight with the
sentences.zh: 当然，这将是罗马随后与迦太基人进行的战争中的一个核心主题。

sentences.en: Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, it's like the Hydra.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就像九头蛇一样。

sentences.en: You chop a head off, another one sprouts back up.
sentences.zh: 你砍掉一个头，另一个头又会长出来。

sentences.en: But at this point, with the whole of Italy successfully pacified, with Pyrrhus seen off, conditions between Rome and Carthage remain stable.
sentences.zh: 但此时，随着整个意大利被成功平定，随着皮洛士被驱逐，罗马和迦太基之间的关系依然保持稳定。

sentences.en: The Carthaginians are not opposed to Rome conquering Italy.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人并不反对罗马征服意大利。

sentences.en: In fact, 348, so this is right when they're just about to embark on their great series of conquests and they've started fighting the Samnites.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在公元前348年，也就是他们正准备开始一系列伟大征服并且已经开始与萨姆尼姆人作战的时候。

sentences.en: The Romans win a particular battle over the Samnites and the Carthaginians send them a tremendously lavish golden crown, which the Romans then keep on the capital as a kind
sentences.zh: 罗马人在对萨姆尼姆人的一场战役中获胜，迦太基人送给他们一顶极其奢华的金冠，罗马人后来把这顶金冠作为一种纪念物保留在卡庇托利山上。

sentences.en: of a memento.
sentences.zh: 的一个纪念品。

sentences.en: And there are definitely Carthaginians in Rome at this point.
sentences.zh: 此时罗马境内确实有迦太基人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there's an entire area of Rome that's called the Vicus Africus, the African quarter on the
sentences.zh: 因此，罗马有一个整片区域被称为维库斯·阿弗里库斯，即埃斯奎林山上的非洲人区。

sentences.en: Esquiline Hill, named after the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 以迦太基人命名。

sentences.en: And the Latin word for market, which is macellum, seems to derive from the Phoenician.
sentences.zh: 而拉丁语中意为市场的词“macellum”，似乎源自腓尼基语。

sentences.en: And there are even vague hints in later Roman writers that there's a betel, which is a kind of sacred stone erected in the fruit market in Rome.
sentences.zh: 后来的罗马作家甚至隐约暗示，罗马的水果市场里竖立着一块贝特尔石，这是一种神圣的石头。

sentences.en: So there is a Carthaginian presence.
sentences.zh: 所以确实存在迦太基人的足迹。

sentences.en: As per the terms of the treaty, Carthaginian merchants are moving freely around Rome and the cities that are subordinate to Rome.
sentences.zh: 根据条约条款，迦太基商人正在罗马以及从属于罗马的城市中自由活动。

sentences.en: And just one last thing on Carthage.
sentences.zh: 关于迦太基，最后还有一件事。

sentences.en: What have they been doing all this time?
sentences.zh: 他们这段时间都在干什么？

sentences.en: So there's just been presumably a succession of people called Mago and Hanno and stuff, just interchangeably kind of making loads of money.
sentences.zh: 所以大概有一连串名叫马戈和汉诺之类的人，像走马灯一样不断地赚取大量的金钱。

sentences.en: They have been fighting the Syracusans.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在与叙拉古人作战。

sentences.en: Ah, okay.
sentences.zh: 啊，好吧。

sentences.en: Which we talked about in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集中讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: In the wake of that, they've been licking their wounds.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，他们一直在舔舐伤口。

sentences.en: They've been trying to, you know, rebuild their forces, hire more mercenaries, build up their fleet.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在努力，你知道的，重建他们的军队，招募更多的雇佣兵，扩建他们的舰队。

sentences.en: And so this is why when Pyrrhus comes, a Greek king, the Carthaginians assume that Pyrrhus is the major enemy.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么当皮洛士这个希腊国王到来时，迦太基人认为皮洛士是主要的敌人。

sentences.en: And this is why they're happy to be in alliance with the Romans.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们很高兴能与罗马人结盟。

sentences.en: They don't think of the Romans as being a threat comparable to Pyrrhus.
sentences.zh: 他们不认为罗马人是堪比皮洛士的威胁。

sentences.en: Essentially because the Carthaginians, like the Greeks in Sicily and like everybody in
sentences.zh: 主要是因为迦太基人，就像西西里的希腊人和意大利的每个人一样，他们需要时间来摸清他们在罗马面对的到底是什么。

sentences.en: Italy, it takes time for them to work out what they're facing in Rome.
sentences.zh: 西地中海每个人都接受了一种作战规则。

sentences.en: There are kind of rules of combat that everyone in the Western Mediterranean has accepted.
sentences.zh: 它可能非常残酷。

sentences.en: It can be very brutal.
sentences.zh: 城市可能会被毁灭等等。

sentences.en: Cities can be destroyed or whatever.
sentences.zh: 但大体上，这并没有发生。
